source.title: How does Architecture Influence the Base Capabilities of Pre-trained Language Models? A Case Study Based on FFN-Wider and MoE Transformers
source.authors: Xin Lu; Yan-Yan Zhao; Bing Qin; Liangyu Huo; Qing Yang; Dongliang Xu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether architectural changes affect language-model loss and base capabilities using architecture comparisons, rather than testing the original scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The study cites scaling laws but does not fit or test power laws in parameters, tokens, or compute, and does not test compute-optimal allocation. Pretraining validation losses are used to align or select models, so they are not recorded as findings. Downstream task results do not test the claim versions about scaling-law predictability.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture study, not a scaling-law study. Only one result bears on V4. In the MoE experiment, two 14B models (1.5B activated) with the same compute and 100B tokens differ only in where the MoE layer sits. Their in-distribution loss differs slightly (2.315 vs 2.303). In the FFN-Wider vs CAA comparisons, in-distribution loss was aligned by construction, so it is not a finding. The Pile and SlimPajama out-of-distribution losses measure transfer to other distributions, not held-out pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the contribution ratio of MHA (a combination function) to pre-trained language modeling is a key factor in base capabilities. FFN-Wider Transformers lower that ratio, which degrades out-of-distribution language modeling, transfer and few-shot performance at aligned pretraining loss. Their proposed fix, CEA, reverses the decline in BERT and GPT and improves a 14B MoE model at the same parameters, compute and steps.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates architecture changes rather than reproducing scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary with architecture configuration and model family; the authors report an anomalous GPT result when the Outer-FFN is removed. MoE OOD losses also vary by evaluation dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched in-distribution loss, parameters, compute and steps, architecture changes shift out-of-distribution loss. The shift is small for the CAA models on Pile (e.g. -3.256 vs -3.203 log-likelihood). It is larger for MoE CEA on SlimPajama subsets, up to about 6% (Book 2.761 vs 2.585; Wiki 3.155 vs 2.964).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameters, compute and in-distribution loss, architecture choices (the share of contribution from attention vs FFN) change out-of-distribution loss and downstream capabilities beyond what in-distribution loss predicts.

record.problems: The architecture comparisons cover selected BERT, GPT, and MoE configurations rather than a broad architecture sweep. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated losses.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream task scores were not extracted because they do not test the claim versions about scaling-law loss or downstream predictability. Results in the main setting that do not state parameter-count alignment were not included as fixed-parameter architecture comparisons.

untested.parts: No power-law fits in parameters, tokens or compute.
No depth, width or aspect-ratio sweeps at fixed parameter count. Only one MoE placement change is tested, at a single scale.
No other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream scores are compared across architectures at a matched scale, not as a function of scale or loss.

missing.what: In-distribution SlimPajama-CC&C4 loss: Vanilla MoE 14B 2.315 vs MoE 14B w/ CEA 2.303, at the same parameters, compute and 100B tokens. Bears on V4 with state observed (small change).

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 labels rested on out-of-distribution loss rows. In r1–r4, in-distribution loss was aligned by choosing the width ratio, so those rows cannot show V4's effect. The one V4-relevant result, the MoE in-distribution loss, is unrecorded. Treating out-of-distribution loss as outside V4 is a judgement call. If the project counts transfer loss under V4, the MoE rows (up to about 6% differences) would instead suggest limits_scope.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law loss relationships in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation trends.
The study tests selected architecture comparisons, not a broad range of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and training regimes such as repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Sensitivity of fitted scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits to setup or fitting choices.
